His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿while they do not perceive﴾ admits of two meanings.

One of them: an emphasis on the meaning of His saying "suddenly," as one says: "I came upon him in a state of heedlessness, in such a way that he did not know," so His saying "in such a way that he did not know" emphasizes the meaning of heedlessness.

The second: it is a statement that conveys an independent benefit, namely that the punishment comes upon them suddenly while they do not perceive this matter, and they suppose that the punishment will not come upon them at all.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell is encompassing the disbelievers.﴾ This was mentioned as an expression of wonder. The reason is that one who is threatened with a matter involving slight harm, such as a slap or a punch, feels bold within himself and says, "In the name of God, bring it on!" As for one who is threatened with drowning or burning, and is certain that the one threatening him is able and does not break his promise, it does not occur to any sensible person to say to him, "Bring what you threaten me with!" Here He says: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment﴾, and the punishment is the Fire of Hell encompassing them. So His saying ﴿They ask you to hasten﴾ is first an informing about them, and second an expression of wonder at them. Then He mentioned how Hell encompasses them, saying, exalted is He:

﴿On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, and He will say: "Taste what you used to do."﴾

Regarding this there are two issues:

The first issue: Why did He single out the two sides for mention and did not mention the right, the left, behind, and in front? We say: Because the purpose is to mention what distinguishes the Fire of Hell from the fire of this world. The fire of this world encompasses the four sides, for whoever enters it has flames behind him, in front of him, to his right and to his left. As for fire from above, it does not descend; rather, under ordinary circumstances it rises from below. And beneath the feet, the flame that is under a foot does not remain. But the Fire of Hell descends from above and is not extinguished by stepping on the place of the foot.

Page 73
The second issue: He said ﴿from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ and did not say "from above their heads," nor "from above them and from beneath them." Rather, He mentioned the thing added to when mentioning "beneath" and did not mention it when mentioning "above." We say: Because the descent of the Fire from above, whether it comes from the direction of the heads or from another place, is wondrous; therefore He did not restrict it to the head. As for the remaining of the Fire beneath the foot, that alone is wondrous, since otherwise flames do occur on the sides of the foot in this world while they are beneath it. So He mentioned the wondrous thing, which is what is beneath the feet, since He did not mention trampling, nor what is above in absolute terms.
* * *
Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿and He will say: "Taste what you used to do."﴾ When He explained the punishment of their bodies, He explained the punishment of their souls, which is that it will be said to them, as a means of humiliation and disgrace: "Taste the punishment of what you used to do." He made that the very thing they used to do, for emphasis, by way of applying the name of the cause to the effect, since their deeds were a cause for God making them a cause of their punishment. This is very common in usage.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is vast, so worship Me alone.﴾

The connection (wajh al-ta'alluq) is that when God, exalted is He, mentioned the state of the polytheists separately and the state of the People of the Book separately, and combined them in the warning and made them among the people of the Fire, their obstinacy intensified, their corruption grew, and they strove to harm the believers and prevented them from worship. So He addressed the believers, saying: ﴿O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is vast, so worship Me alone.﴾ If worship becomes impossible for you in some part of it, then emigrate, and do not abandon My worship under any circumstance. From this it is known that remaining in the land of war (dar al-harb) is forbidden and leaving it is obligatory; so that even if a man swears by divorce that he will not leave, he is obliged to leave, and he is restrained until the divorce takes effect. Then, in the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: ﴿O My servants﴾ intends only address to the believers, even though the disbeliever is included in His saying ﴿O My servants﴾. We say: he is not included in His saying ﴿O My servants﴾, for several reasons:

One of them: whoever is addressed as "My servants" (ʿibadi) has no authority over him by Satan, based on the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, over My servants you have no authority﴾ [al-Hijr: 42]. The disbeliever is under the authority of Satan, so he is not included in His saying ﴿O My servants﴾.

The second: the address "My servants" is the most noble station of the responsible person (mukallaf). This is because when God created Adam, He gave him a great name, which is the name of khilafa (vicegerency), as God said: ﴿Indeed, I am placing a khalifa on earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. The khalifa is the greatest of people in rank and the most complete of those possessing power in capability. Then Iblis was not intimidated by this name and was not defeated; rather he advanced against it because of it, opposed it, and overcame it, as God said: ﴿So Satan caused them to slip﴾ [al-Baqarah: 36]. Then among his righteous descendants are those named "My servants," so Satan withdrew from them and shrank, as God said: ﴿Indeed, over My servants you have no authority﴾, and he said with his own tongue: ﴿I will surely mislead them all﴾ ﴿except Your servants among them﴾ [Sad: 82–83]. Thus it is known that the responsible person, when he is a servant of God, is higher in rank than when he is a khalifa over the face of the earth. Perhaps Adam, like Dawud about whom God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, We have made you a khalifa on the earth﴾ [Sad: 26], did not escape the hand of Satan except at the time when God, exalted is He, said of him "My servant," and when He called him with the words: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves﴾ [al-A'raf: 23], and chose him by this call, just as He said concerning Dawud: ﴿And remember Our servant Dawud, the possessor of strength﴾ [Sad: 17]. If this is known, then the disbeliever is not fit for vicegerency, so how is he fit for what is greater than vicegerency? Therefore none enters into His saying ﴿O My servants﴾ except the believer.

The third: this address was obtained by the believer through his own striving with God's enabling, because God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Call upon Me, I will respond to you﴾ [Ghafir: 60]. The believer called upon his Lord by saying: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith, "Believe in your Lord," so we believed﴾ [Al 'Imran: 193]. So God answered him by saying: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God"﴾ [al-Zumar: 53]. The relation between God and the servant, through the servant's saying "my God" and God's saying "My servant," was confirmed by the servant's supplication. But the disbeliever did not supplicate, so he was not answered; therefore ﴿O My servants﴾ does not encompass anyone other than the believers.

The second issue: if "My servants" applies only to believers, what is the benefit of His saying ﴿who have believed﴾? The attribute is mentioned for distinguishing the described, as one says "O responsible people who are believers" and "O wise men," to distinguish them from disbelievers and the ignorant. We say: the attribute is mentioned not for distinction but merely to show that the attribute is present in them, as one says: "the honored prophets" and "the purified angels," though every prophet is honored and every angel is purified; it is said only to show that honor and purity are present in them. Similar to this is our saying: "God the Mighty" and "Zayd the tall." Here it is mentioned to show that they are believers.

The third issue: since He said ﴿O My servants﴾, they are worshippers, so what is the benefit of the command to worship in His saying "so worship Me"? We say: there are two benefits in it. The first: constancy (al-mudawama), meaning: O you who worshipped Me in the past, worship Me in the future. The second: sincerity (al-ikhlas), meaning: O you who worship Me, make your action sincere for Me and do not worship other than Me.

The fourth issue: the fa' in His saying ﴿so Me﴾ (fa-iyyaya) indicates that it is an answer to a condition. What is that? We say: His saying ﴿Indeed, My earth is vast﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 56] is an indication of the absence of an obstacle to His worship. It is as if He said: if there is no obstacle to My worship, then worship Me. As for the fa' in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so worship Me﴾, it is for the ordering of the consequence upon the cause, as one says: "this is a scholar, so honor him." Likewise here: when He made Himself known by saying ﴿so Me﴾, and He, by Himself, deserves worship, He said: ﴿so worship Me﴾.

The fifth issue: the servant said something similar in His saying ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5] and followed it with ﴿and You alone we seek help﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5]. God agreed with him in His saying ﴿so Me alone worship﴾ and did not mention help. We say: rather, it is mentioned in His saying ﴿O My servants﴾, because what is meant by "My servants," when Satan is cut off from the path to them and cut off from their tribe, is in the utmost help.

The sixth issue: God put help first and the servant put seeking help later. We say: because the servant's act is for a purpose, and every act done for a purpose, the purpose precedes the act in perception. This is because one who builds a house for dwelling first conceives the benefit of dwelling, which moves him to build; but the purpose does not come into existence except after the intermediate act is performed. So we say: the seeking of help by the servant is for the purpose of worship, so it precedes in his perception. As for God, exalted is He, His act is not for a purpose, so He observed the order of existence, for help precedes worship.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 29, verse 57:

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned.﴾

When God, exalted is He, commanded the believers to emigrate (al-muhajarah), it was hard for them to leave their homelands and to part from their brothers. So He told them that what they dislike must necessarily befall them, for ﴿every soul shall taste death﴾, and death separates loved ones. It is therefore better that it occur in the way of God, so that He may reward you for it, for to God is your return. There is also a subtler and more refined aspect: God, exalted is He, said, "Every soul, when it is not attached to anything other than itself, is subject to death, and then to God it returns, so it does not die," as He said: ﴿They will not taste death therein﴾ [al-Dukhan: 56]. Given this, whoever wishes not to taste death does not remain attached to his own self, for the self is the one who tastes death; rather, he attaches himself to something other than it. If that other is other than God, then it is subject to death and destined for destruction, by His saying: ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾ and ﴿Everything is perishing except His Face﴾ [al-Qasas: 88]. Thus attachment to God relieves one from death. So God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So worship Me alone﴾, that is, attach yourselves to Me and do not follow the self, for it is subject to death. ﴿Then to Us you will be returned﴾, that is, when you are attached to Me, your death is a return to Me and not a death, as He said: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of God as dead; rather, they are alive﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169]. And he, peace be upon him, said: "The believers do not die; rather, they are transferred from one abode to another." In light of this aspect too, the meaning of attachment becomes clear.

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely settle them in lofty chambers in Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. How excellent is the reward of the workers.﴾

He explained what the believers will have at the time of their return to Him, just as He had earlier explained what the disbelievers will have, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 54]. So He explained that the believers will have the Gardens (al-Jinan) in contrast to the Fire that the disbelievers will have. He also explained that in them are chambers (ghuraf) beneath which rivers flow, in contrast to the statement that the Fire is beneath the disbelievers. And He explained that this is the reward of their deeds by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾, in contrast to His explanation that what preceded is the recompense of the deeds of the disbelievers by His saying: ﴿Taste what you used to do﴾.

Between the two verses there are differences, which contain subtle points. Among them: He, exalted, mentioned in the punishment that above them is a punishment, i.e., fire, but He did not mention here anything above them. Instead He mentioned what is above them without any addition, namely the chambers (al-ghurf). This is because what is mentioned in both places is physical punishment and physical reward. But the disbeliever is in the lowest level of the Fire, so above him are layers of Fire. As for the believers, they will be in the highest of 'Illiyyin, so He did not mention anything above them, as an indication of the loftiness of their rank and the elevation of their station.

* * *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For them are chambers, above them are chambers﴾ [Az-Zumar: 20], this does not contradict that, because the chambers above the chambers are not above them, whereas the Fire above the Fire is above them. Another point is that there He mentioned the Fire beneath their feet, whereas here He mentioned water beneath their chambers. This is because fire does not cause pain when it is beneath a person in general, so long as it is not directly beneath the feet and connected to them. But if the flame is inclined away from the direction of the foot, even though it is beneath it, or is directly beneath but not adjacent to it, rather lower in a pit, it does not cause pain. As for water, when it is beneath the chamber in any way and at any distance, it is pleasant to him. So He said regarding the Fire, beneath their feet, so that pain would result from it, and He said here, beneath the chambers, so that pleasure would result from it however it is. Another point is that there He said ﴿Taste﴾ to inflict pain upon their hearts by the form of the imperative, whereas here He said ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾ to gladden their hearts, not in the form of an imperative. This is because the imperative form indicates the cessation of the connection after it. For whoever says to his hired worker, "Take your wage," it is understood from it that by this his connection to him is severed. But when one says, "How excellent is your wage with me," or "How excellent is your wealth of reward," it is understood from it that this remains with him. Here He did not say, "Take your wages, O workers," whereas there He said: ﴿Taste what you used to do﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 55]. If someone says: if "taste" implies cessation, then the punishment of the disbeliever would end. We say: that is not so, because when God says "taste," it indicates that He has given them their recompense and the connection between Him and them has ended, but that this remains upon them permanently, neither decreasing nor increasing. As for the believer, when He gives him something, He does not withdraw it along with what He has given him; rather He increases for him every day in blessings. To this refers His saying: ﴿For those who do good is the best [reward] and an increase﴾ [Yunus: 26]. That is, what reaches the disbeliever continues without increase, whereas what reaches the believer increases continually. As for eternity (al-khulud), although it is not mentioned in regard to the disbeliever, that is known from other texts.

[Page 76]

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who are patient and upon their Lord they rely.﴾

He mentioned two matters, patience (al-sabr) and reliance (al-tawakkul), because time is past, present and future. But the past cannot be remedied, and the servant is not commanded to do anything regarding it. The present remains, and what is fitting for it is patience; the future remains, and what is fitting for it is reliance. So he is patient over the harm that befalls him in the present, and he relies upon God regarding what he needs in the future.

Know that patience and reliance are two qualities that are not attained except with knowledge of God and knowledge of what is other than God. Whoever knows what is other than God knows that it is transient, so patience becomes easy for him, since patience over what is transient is light. And whoever knows God knows that He is everlasting, who brings him his provisions; so if something escapes him, he relies upon the Living, the Everlasting. The mention of patience and reliance here is appropriate, for His saying: ﴿O My servants﴾ was to clarify that there is no obstacle to worship, and whoever is harmed in one land should leave it. So people fall into two categories: one able to leave, who relies upon his Lord, abandoning homelands and parting from brothers; and one unable, who is patient in bearing harm and persistent in the worship of God, exalted is He.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision; God provides for it and for you. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

When He mentioned "those who are patient and upon their Lord they rely," He mentioned what helps in reliance, which is the explanation of the condition of the animals that store nothing for tomorrow, yet each day there comes to them abundant provision. In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: regarding *ka'ayyin* (how many), there are four dialects, and no others: this one, *ka'in* on the pattern of *ra'in*, *ka'yin* on the pattern of *rayn*, and *kay* on the pattern of *da'*. Only *ka'ayyin* was recited, and *ka'in* is the reading of Ibn Kathir.

The second issue: *ka'ayyin* is a compound word made of the particle of comparison *ka* and *ayyin*, which is used in the manner of *man* and *ma*, and the compound was made to mean *kam* (how many). It was written only with a *nun* in order to distinguish the compound from the non-compound; for *ka'ayyin* is used uncompounded, as the speaker says: "I saw a man, not *ka'ayyi rajulin yakun*," so the genitive complement has been omitted, and one says: "I saw a man, not *ka'ayyi rajulin*," and then *ka'ayyin* is not compound. When it is compound here, it is written with the *nun* to distinguish it, just as *Ma'dikarib* and *Ba'labakk* are written, and as *thamma* is written with a *ha'* to distinguish it from *thumma*.

The third issue: *ka'ayyin* in the sense of *kam* is rarely used with *min*, whereas *kam* is frequently used without *min*; one says *kam rajulan* and *kam min rajulin*. That is because of the distinction we have explained between *ka'ayyin* in the sense of *kam* and the uncompounded *ka'ayyi*, for when *ka'ayyi* is uncompounded it is not permissible to place *min* after it, since one does not say "I saw a man, not *ka'ayyi min rajulin*"; whereas the compounded form in the sense of *kam* permits this, so it was made obligatory for the sake of distinction.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿does not carry its provision﴾: it was said: it does not carry it because of its weakness; it was said: it refers to lice, fleas, worms and the like; and it was said: it does not store. ﴿God provides for it and for you﴾ by way of analogy, meaning: there is no doubt that its provision is none other than from God, so likewise He provides for you; so rely upon Him. If someone says: whoever says that God provides for the animals, rather the plants in the desert are caused, and the animal goes to them and grazes, we say: the proof for this is from three aspects, considering the provision, considering the one who is provided for, and considering the totality of the provision and the one provided for.

As for considering the provision: God, exalted is He, had He not created plants, there would be no provision for the animal.

As for considering the one provided for: nourishment is not merely swallowing; rather it must cling to the organs until the grass becomes bone, flesh and fat, and this is only by the wisdom of God, exalted is He, in that He created within it an attracting faculty, a retaining faculty, a digestive faculty, an expelling faculty and other powers, and by the pure power and will of God; so it is He who provides for it.

As for considering the one provided for and the provision together: had God not guided the animal to food so that it recognizes it by smell, nourishment would not take place for it. Do you not see that among animals there are some that do not recognize a kind of food until it is forced into their mouth so that they taste it and then eat it afterwards? For often the camel does not recognize leaven or barley until it is fed two or three times, and then it recognizes it and eats it afterwards. If someone says: how is it valid to analogize man to animals in what requires reliance, when the animal's provision is not interfered with, if it eats some of it today and leaves the remainder which it finds tomorrow, no one extends a hand to it; whereas if man does not take today, nothing remains for him tomorrow? And also, man's needs are many, for he needs kinds of clothing and varieties of food, while the animal does not; and also the animal's sustenance is prepared, whereas man's sustenance requires toil, such as sowing, harvesting, grinding and baking; so if he does not gather it before the need, he would not find it at the time of need. We say: we do not say that gathering damages reliance; rather the one who sows and harvests may be reliant, and the one who bows and prostrates may be non-reliant. For whoever sows, his dependence is upon God, and his belief in God is that if He wills, He provides without sowing, and if He wills, He does not provide from that sowing; so he works while his heart is with God, and he is truly reliant. Whoever prays while his heart is with what is in the hand of Zayd and 'Amr is not reliant.

As for his saying: man's needs are many, we say his means of earning are also many: he earns with his hand, like the tailor and the weaver; with his foot, like the courier and others; with his eye, like the watchman; with his tongue, like the driver of camels and the caller; with his understanding, like the engineer and the merchant; with his knowledge, like the physician and the jurist; with the strength of his body, like the porter and the carrier. The animal has no means of earning. So the loaf of bread that man needs tomorrow or the day after is far-fetched that God would not provide it with these means; therefore he is more deserving of reliance.

Also, God, exalted is He, created man such that provision and its causes come to him; for God has made man possessor of the wealth of this world and has arranged it so that it enters his possession whether he wills or not, to the extent that the offspring of livestock and the fruits of trees enter into ownership even if the owner of the cattle and trees does not intend it; and when one generation dies, that passes to another generation by compulsion, whether they will or not. The condition of the animal is not like this at all, for if the animal does not go to provision, its provision does not come to it. Thus man, if he relies, would be closer to reason than the reliance of the animal.

Then He said: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: All-Hearing when you seek provision, He hears and responds; All-Knowing if you remain silent, your need and the measure of your need are not hidden from Him.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if you ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?", they will surely say, "Allah." So how are they turned away?﴾

We say: When Allah made the matter clear to the polytheist, addressing him directly, and he did not benefit from it and turned away from it, and He addressed the believer with His words, ﴿O My servants who have believed﴾, and completed the speech with him, He mentioned along with it what would serve as guidance for the polytheist, in such a way that he would hear it. This is a method of the utmost excellence. If a master has two slaves, or a father has two sons, one of whom is upright and the other corrupt, he first advises the corrupt one. If he does not listen, he turns away from him, addressing the upright one: "This one does not deserve to be spoken to. So listen, you, and do not be like this corrupt one." This speech thus contains both the advice of the reformer and the rebuke of the corrupt one, for his saying that this one does not deserve to be addressed causes distress in his heart. Then, if he mentions the reformer in the course of the speech while the corrupt one is listening, saying: "This is your brother, and it is astonishing of him that he knows the ugliness of his action, recognises corruption from righteousness, and the path of guidance and success, and yet occupies himself with its opposite," this speech also serves as a summons for the corrupt one to the path of guidance and a barrier preventing him from that corruption. Likewise, Allah the Exalted said, addressing the believer: "It is astonishing of them that if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, 'Allah,' and yet they do not believe."

There are subtle points in the verse:

First: He mentioned creation in relation to the heavens and the earth, and subjection in relation to the sun and the moon. This is because the mere creation of the sun and the moon is not a wisdom, for if the sun were created in such a way that it remained in one place and did not move, there would be no night and day, no summer and no winter. Therefore the wisdom lies in their movement and their subjection.

Second: Concerning the word "subjection" (taskhīr): movement indicates mere motion, and mere motion is not sufficient, for if they moved as we move, they would not traverse the celestial orb (falak) in thousands of years. The wisdom in their subjection is that they move, within the time a person takes to breathe, through thousands of farsakhs. Then He did not make for them a single motion but several motions. One is their movement from east to west once every day and night. The other is their movement from west to east, and the evidence for it is that the crescent is seen on the western horizon at a specific distance from the sun, and then it recedes from it toward the east until the moon is seen at the middle of the month opposite the sun, with the sun on the western horizon and the moon on the eastern horizon. And there is another motion: the motion of the apogee (awj), and the motion of the inclination (māʾil) and the epicycle (tadwīr) of the moon. Had it not been for the motion from west to east, the seasons would not have come about.

Then know that the astronomers (aṣḥāb al-hay'a, i.e. those of astronomy) said: the sun is fixed in the orb (falak), and the orb turns it by its rotation. The exegetes of the outward meaning (al-mufassirūn al-ẓāhiriyyūn) denied this. We say: there is no impossibility in that, if they do not hold to nature (ṭabīʿa), for Allah the Exalted is a free-choosing agent. If He wills to move them within the orb while the orb is still, it is permissible; and if He wills to move them by the motion of the orb while they are at rest, that is also permissible, and there is no decisive or clear text concerning it. We will mention the full discussion in His words: ﴿And each in an orbit they swim﴾ [Yā Sīn: 40].

Third: He mentioned two matters, one being the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the other being the subjection of the sun and the moon, because bringing into existence may pertain to essences (dhawāt) and may pertain to attributes (ṣifāt). The creation of the heavens and the earth is an indication of bringing essences into existence, and the subjection of the sun and the moon is an indication of bringing attributes into existence, namely motion and other things. Thus it is as though He mentioned two examples from the two categories. Then He said: ﴿So how are they turned away?﴾, meaning: they believe this, so how are they turned away from the worship of Allah, when whoever's greatness is known, his service is obligatory? There is no greatness above the greatness of the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and no baseness below the baseness of inanimate matter, for inanimate matter is lower than animals, animals are lower than humans, and humans are lower than the inhabitants of the heavens. How, then, do they abandon the worship of the greatest of existents and occupy themselves with the worship of the basest of existents?

[Page 79]

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿God extends provision to whom He wills of His servants, and restricts it for him. Indeed God is Knower of all things.﴾

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God extends provision to whom He wills of His servants﴾. When He had explained creation, He mentioned provision, because the perfection of creation lies in its sustenance, and a human being's survival is by provision. So He said: the one who is worshipped is either worshipped because he deserves worship, and these idols are not so, while God deserves it; or because of his being upon the rightful state (al-sha'n), and God, who created the heavens and the earth in the rightful manner, is clear in proof, so worship is due to Him; or because of his being the Patron of benefaction, and God provides for creation, so to Him belong bounty, benevolence, grace and favour, and therefore worship is due to Him from this aspect too.

His saying: ﴿to whom He wills﴾ is an indication of the perfection of benevolence. That is because when a king orders the treasurer to give a person something, and he gives it, there is for him a gift that is small and insignificant, since the recipient says: this is not by his own will, but by the command of the king. But if the king acts by choice, saying to him: if you wish, give it, and if you wish, do not give it, then if he gives it, there is for him a gift that is great, not small. So God, exalted is He, said: provision is from Him and by His will, so it is complete benevolence that demands complete gratitude.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and restricts it for him﴾, that is, He narrows it for him if He wills. Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed God is Knower of all things﴾, that is, He knows the measures of needs and the measures of provisions. Concerning the affirmation of knowledge here, there are subtleties:

The first: the Provider, who has perfect will, when He sees His servant in need and knows his hunger, does not delay provision from him. The Provider delays provision only because of a deficiency in the execution of His will, like a king who wishes to feed, but the food has not yet been prepared, or because of his lack of knowledge of the hunger of the servants.

The second: by affirming knowledge, God has comprehended the mention of the attributes that are the attributes of the Deity, and whoever denies them is a disbeliever. They are four: life, power, will and knowledge. As for hearing, sight and the speech subsisting in Him, whoever denies them is an innovator (mubtadi') and not a disbeliever. He has completed the four, because His saying: ﴿who created the heavens and the earth﴾ is an indication of the perfection of power; His saying: ﴿extends provision to whom He wills﴾ is an indication of the execution of His will and volition; His saying: ﴿Indeed God is Knower of all things﴾ is an indication of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge; and the one who is powerful, willing and knowing cannot be conceived except as living. Then, when He, exalted is He, said: ﴿God extends provision﴾, He mentioned their acknowledgment of this, so He said:

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 29, verse 63:

﴿And if you asked them, "Who sends down water from the sky and with it gives life to the earth after its death?", they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Praise be to Allah." But most of them do not reason.﴾

That is, this is the cause of provision, and the one who brings the cause into being brings the effect into being. So provision is from Allah. Then He said, ﴿Say, "Praise be to Allah"﴾, and this may have several meanings:

The first: it is an interjected statement within a discourse, as if He said: "and He gives life with it to the earth after its death," then, in the midst of this speech, ﴿Praise be to Allah﴾ is mentioned for the sake of recalling the blessing, as the poet said:

"Indeed the eighty, and I have reached them, have made my hearing in need of an interpreter."

The second: the intended meaning is a continuous discourse, namely that they know that this is from Allah and acknowledge it, but they do not act on what they know. You know and act, and so do the believers who follow you. So say, "Praise be to Allah," and most of them do not understand that all praise belongs to Allah, so they praise other than Allah for a blessing that is from Allah.

The third: the intended meaning is that they say it is from Allah, yet they also say that other than Allah is divine, so the contradiction in their statement and the incoherence of their doctrine becomes evident. So ﴿Say, "Praise be to Allah"﴾ upon the manifestation of their contradiction, ﴿and most of them do not reason﴾ this contradiction, or the corruption of this contradiction.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and play. And indeed, the Hereafter—that is the [true] life, if they only knew.﴾

When He had made clear that they acknowledge God as the Creator and the Provider, yet they abandon His worship, and they do not abandon it except for the adornment of the worldly life, He made clear that what they incline towards is not a thing of substance, by His saying: ﴿And this worldly life is nothing but amusement﴾. In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: What is the difference between lahw (amusement) and la'ib (play), such that it is correct to conjoin one with the other? We say: the difference is in two respects:

The first: every occupation that is undertaken—when the responsible person turns to it, he is bound to turn away from other things. And the one whom no affair distracts from another affair is God, exalted is He. So whoever turns to falsehood for a small, passing pleasure in it is bound to turn away from the truth. Thus, turning to falsehood is play (la'ib), and turning away from the truth is amusement (lahw). So the worldly life is play, i.e., turning to falsehood, and amusement, i.e., turning away from the truth.

The second: the one occupied with a thing necessarily prefers that thing over others, until he engages in it. Either this preference is in the manner of precedence, by saying "I give priority to this, and that other I will do afterwards," or it is in the manner of total absorption in it and turning away from everything else entirely. The first is play, and the second is amusement. The evidence for this is that chess, pigeons, and what is close to them are not called instruments of amusement (ālāt al-malāhī) in common usage, whereas the lute (ʿūd) and other stringed instruments are called instruments of amusement, because they divert a person from other things due to the immediate pleasure in them. So the worldly life is play for some, who occupy themselves with it and say after this occupation, "I will occupy myself with worship and the Hereafter," and it is amusement for others, who occupy themselves with it and forget the Hereafter entirely.

The second issue: God, exalted is He, said in Surat al-An'am: ﴿And what is the worldly life﴾, and He did not say "And what is this worldly life." Here He said: "And this (wa-hadhihi)." We say: because what was mentioned previously here is the matter of the world, where He said: ﴿So He gives life by it to the earth after its death﴾, so He said "this." And what was mentioned before it there is the Hereafter, where He said: ﴿Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it, while they bear their burdens upon their backs﴾ [al-An'am: 31]. So at that time the world was not in their minds, so He said: ﴿And what is the worldly life﴾.

The third issue: He said there: ﴿nothing but play and amusement﴾, and He said here: ﴿nothing but amusement and play﴾. We say: since what was mentioned there previously was the Hereafter and their display of regret, at that moment total absorption in the world is remote, rather the mere act of occupation with it is [remote]; so He postponed the more remote [element]. But here, since what was mentioned previously was the world, which is deceptive and calls souls to turn to it and be absorbed in it, unless there is a preventer that prevents him from total absorption, so he occupies himself with it without total absorption in it, or a protector that protects him so he does not occupy himself with it at all, total absorption here was nearer than its absence, so He placed amusement first.

The fourth issue: He said there: ﴿And the Abode of the Hereafter is better﴾ [al-An'am: 32], and He said here: ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter—that is the [true] life﴾. We say: since the situation there was one of displaying regret, the responsible person did not need a strong deterrent, so He said "the Hereafter is better." And since the situation here is one of occupation with the world, he needed a strong deterrent, so He said "there is no life except the life of the Hereafter." This is like when a rational person is presented with two things and says of one, "this is better than that," which is merely preference; but if he says, "this is good, and that other is nothing," it is preference with emphasis. Likewise here He emphasized, because the responsible person is deeply immersed in the world.

The fifth issue: He said there: ﴿better for those who are wary [of God]﴾ [al-An'am: 32], and He did not say here "except that it is the [true] life," because the Hereafter is better only for the one who is wary (al-muttaqi), i.e., wary of shirk. As for the disbeliever, the world is his paradise, so it is better for him than the Hereafter. As for the Hereafter being everlasting, in which is the lasting life, this is not restricted to one people over another.

The sixth issue: How is the word hayawan (animal/living being) applied to the Hereafter, when hayawan refers to a growing, perceiving creature? We say: hayawan is a verbal noun from "hayya" (to live), like hayah (life), but it carries an intensification not found in hayah. The intended meaning of "the Hereafter" is the second life, so it is as if He said: the second life is the life that truly counts. Or we say: since in the Hereafter there is increase and growth, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿For those who did good is the best [reward] and an increase﴾ [Yunus: 26], and since it is the place of complete and true perception, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The Day when secrets are tested﴾ [al-Tariq: 9], He applied to it the term used for the growing, perceiving creature.

The seventh issue: In Surat al-An'am He said: ﴿Will you not reason?﴾, and here He said: ﴿if they only knew﴾. This is because what was affirmed there was that the Hereafter is better, and that this is evident and depends only on reason; whereas what is affirmed here is that there is no life except the life of the Hereafter, and this is subtle and is not known except through beneficial knowledge.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, behold, they associate partners [with Him].﴾

This indicates that what prevents monotheism (tawhid) is the worldly life. Its explanation is that when their hope in the world is cut off, they return to the innate disposition (fitrah) that bears witness to monotheism, and they affirm His oneness and become sincere. But when He saves them and grants them respite, they return to what they were upon, the love of the world, and they commit shirk.

* * *

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So that they may disbelieve in what We have given them, and so that they may enjoy themselves; but they will come to know.﴾

There are two aspects to this.

The first: the lam is the lam of purpose (lam kay), meaning: they commit shirk so that their shirk becomes disbelief in the blessing of deliverance, and so that they enjoy themselves through shirk. "But they will come to know" refers to the consequence of their deeds when their hopes vanish.

The second: the lam is the lam of command (lam al-amr), and the meaning is "let them disbelieve" as a threat, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do what you will﴾ [Fussilat: 40], and as He said [Al-An'am: 135]: ﴿Act according to your position; indeed, I am acting. So you will come to know...﴾ the ruin of what you do.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 29, verses 67–68:

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are being snatched away all around them? Do they then believe in falsehood and deny the blessing of God?﴾

The meaning of the verse is clear. What is subtle is how the verse connects to what precedes it. We say: A person at sea is in the state of greatest fear, and in his home he is in the state of greatest safety, especially if his home is in a fortified city. When God mentioned the polytheists' state at the time of great fear, and they saw themselves, in that state, turning back to God, exalted is He, He reminded them of their state at the time of great safety, which is their being in Mecca. It is their city, their land, their dwelling place, and their birthplace. It is fortified by the fortress of God, for everyone around it refrains from fighting whoever is within it. Being within it averts harms from souls and restrains them. The meaning is: at the time you were in the greatest fear, you called upon God, and in the state of greatest safety you have attained, you disbelieved in God. This is contradictory, because your supplication at that time, sincerely directed, was only because you were certain that the blessing comes from God alone. So how can you disbelieve in this great blessing that has come to you, when you have acknowledged that it can only come from God? And the idols, which you were certain in the state of fear offered no security, how can you believe in them in the state of safety?

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾

When God had explained the matters in the manner mentioned, and no one believed in it, He stated that they are the most unjust of all. This is because injustice, as explained, is placing a thing in other than its proper place. If someone places a thing in a place that is not its place, he is unjust. If he places it in a place where it is impossible for that to be its place, he is more unjust, because impossibility is stronger than non-occurrence, for everything that is impossible does not occur, but not everything that does not occur is impossible. God, exalted is He, cannot possibly have a partner, yet they made a partner for Him. If this were done to a sovereign who is independent in his dominion, it would be injustice deserving the painful punishment from the sovereign. So how much more so when a partner is made for One who cannot possibly have a partner? Also, whoever denies a truthful one who is capable of lying is committing injustice, so how is the state of one who denies a truthful one who cannot possibly lie? Therefore, there is no one more unjust than one who lies against God by ascribing partners to Him and denies God in confirming His Prophet, and denies the Prophet in the message of his Lord, and denies the Qur'an sent down from God to the Messenger. It is strange of the polytheists that they accepted what was made of carved wood as divine, yet did not accept one of noble lineage described as a messenger.

The verse may bear another meaning, which is that when God, exalted is He, explained tawhid (the oneness of God), prophethood, and resurrection (hashr), affirmed them, admonished and warned, He said to His Prophet that he should say to the people:

[p. 83]

﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God﴾, meaning: I have brought the message and said that it is from God, and that this is the speech of God, and you have denied me. The situation then revolves between two matters: either I am a fabricator and a false claimant to prophethood if this is from other than God, or you are deniers of the truth if it is from Him. But I acknowledge the everlasting punishment and I know it, so I do not venture into fabrication, because: ﴿Hell is an abode for the disbelievers﴾, and the false claimant to prophethood is a disbeliever. As for you, you have denied me, so Hell is your abode, since it is an abode for the disbelievers. This in that case would be like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed we or you are upon guidance or in clear error﴾.

﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God﴾, meaning: I have brought the message and said that it is from God, and that this is the speech of God, and you have denied me. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who strive for Us—We will surely guide them to Our paths. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.﴾

When He had finished the affirmation and the rebuke, and the disbelievers did not believe, He consoled the hearts of the believers with His saying: ﴿And those who strive for Us—We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾, meaning: whoever strives through obedience, He will guide him to the paths of Paradise. ﴿And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good﴾ is an allusion to His saying: ﴿For those who do good is the best reward and more﴾ [Yunus: 26]. So His saying ﴿We will surely guide them﴾ alludes to "the best reward" (al-husna), and His saying ﴿And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good﴾ alludes to the companionship and nearness that belong to the doer of good, as an increase over his good deeds. There is also another, judgmental (hukmi) interpretation, namely that the meaning is: ﴿And those who strive for Us﴾, i.e., those who reflect upon Our proofs, ﴿We will surely guide them to Our paths﴾, i.e., so that We may produce in them knowledge of Us. To clarify this point, we say: Our companions, the Mutakallimun (theologians), have said that reflection (nazar) is like a condition (shart) for acquired (istidlali) knowledge, and Allah creates in the one who reflects knowledge following his reflection. The philosophers agreed with them in meaning and said: reflection prepares the soul to receive the intelligible form, and when the soul is prepared, knowledge is obtained for it from the overflow (fayd) of the Giver of forms, both corporeal and intellectual. On this view the arrangement is fitting, because when Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the proofs and they did not give them knowledge or faith, He said: "Indeed, they did not reflect, so they were not guided; rather, it is guidance for the God-fearing," those who guard against fanaticism and obstinacy, so they reflect and He guides them. His saying ﴿And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good﴾ is an allusion to a higher degree than inference, as if He, exalted is He, said: Among people there is one who is far off and does not draw near, and they are the disbelievers; among them is one who draws near through reflection and conduct, and He guides and brings him near; and among them is one with whom Allah is, and who is near to Him, knowing things from Him and not knowing them from things, and one who is with a thing and how he seeks it. So His saying ﴿And who is more unjust﴾ alludes to the first; His saying ﴿And those who strive for Us﴾ alludes to the second; and His saying ﴿And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good﴾ alludes to the third.

And Allah knows best the secrets of His Book. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and His blessings be upon our master Muhammad, the Prophet, and his family and all his companions.
